# Atelier

> Domain routers that dispatch agent skills to the right specialist.
> Invoke one router. It pulls in the forty specialists it needs — the user never names a skill again.

Repository: https://github.com/atelier-skills/atelier
Version: 1.0.0 · Licence: MIT · Node 18+

## What this plugin is

Atelier contains **8 router skills**. Each router is a short map of one professional domain:
it knows every specialist skill in that domain, picks the right lead for the job, adds at most
two supporting skills, and hands off to another router when work crosses a boundary.

The plugin ships with **36 specialist skills bundled inside the repository** — every skill whose
upstream was never public, which therefore travels with the plugin rather than being fetched.
The remaining 67 are cloned from public GitHub sources at install time.

Total dependency surface: **118 skills across 8 routers**. Plugin payload: ~8MB.

## Install

Preferred — from the repository, offline-first:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/atelier-skills/atelier
cd atelier
node install.mjs
```

One line, no clone:

```bash
npx atelier install
```

Already have the files (repo unreachable, air-gapped, or downloaded as an archive):

```bash
node install.mjs --root ~/.agents/skills
```

The installer detects the host agent and writes to the correct skill root:

| Agent | Destination |
|---|---|
| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/skills` |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills` |
| generic agents | `~/.agents/skills` |
| cursor | `~/.cursor/skills` |
| codex | `~/.codex/skills` |

Override with `--agent <name>` or `--root <path>`.
**Skills only register at agent startup — restart the agent after installing.**

### Installer flags

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--offline` | Private bundled skills only. Zero network requests. |
| `--check` | Report what would happen. Installs nothing. |
| `--force` | Overwrite existing skills. |
| `--list` | List routers and their dependency counts. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable summary on stdout. |
| `--in-place` | Install the routers into this repo instead of a skill root. |

Install one router: `node install.mjs web-design`

## The routers

| Router | Skills | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `web-design` | 46 | Landing pages, portfolios, redesigns, design systems, UI, scroll/cinematic motion. Routes by job type. |
| `video-production` | 25 | HTML-to-video (HyperFrames) and React video (Remotion). **Routes by input type** — URL, PR, topic, audio, or existing clip. |
| `seo` | 12 | Ordered pipeline: audit → keywords → clustering → competitors → backlinks → AI visibility → report. |
| `backend` | 15 | APIs, data, auth, architecture, refactors, legacy code, issue backlogs. |
| `payments` | 1 + 6 refs | Stripe. Payments, Connect, Billing, Tax, Security, Treasury. |
| `security` | 1 + 8 agents | Repo and diff scanning, verified patch generation, secret redaction. |
| `vibe-code` | 4 | Fast path from a vague idea to something running. Skips heavyweight process by design. |
| `ship-it` | 6 | Process-to-result spine: decide → plan → build → verify → secure → perform → ship. |

## Self-installing behaviour

Each `SKILL.md` contains an `## AI Installation` section generated from `deps.json`. When a
router is invoked on an incomplete stack, the agent is instructed to:

1. run `node install.mjs <router> --check` to find gaps,
2. run `node install.mjs <router>` to fill them,
3. report honestly what is still missing rather than proceeding silently.

**Hosts without plugin or shell support:** the router instructs the agent to name the missing
skills and ask the user to run the command. It is explicitly forbidden from claiming a skill
is available when it is not.

Hosts running opencode additionally load `.opencode/plugins/atelier.ts`, which injects the
router list into the system prompt and detects a router running with a missing dependency.

## Host support

| Host | Skills | Plugin hook | Security subagents |
|---|---|---|---|
| opencode | yes | yes (`atelier.ts`) | yes, auto-installed to `~/.config/opencode/agent` |
| Claude Code | yes | yes (`plugin.json` + `marketplace.json`) | yes, auto-installed |
| cursor / codex / windsurf / gemini | yes | no — fallback path documented | manual |
| anything else | yes, via `--root` | no | manual |

## How skills arrive

There are exactly two paths, and neither is a failure case:

| How | Count | Network | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bundled in the repo** | 36 | none | Skills whose upstream was never public. They ship inside `bundled/skills/` so the plugin is self-contained. |
| **Fetched from upstream** | 67 | yes | Cloned from the declared public GitHub source at install time. |

**Private-origin skills are not a gap.** Where the author's source was never public, the skill
ships inside the repository instead of being fetched. That is the supported path, not a
workaround — and it is why the repo carries them rather than linking out.

Resolution order for every dependency:

```
already installed  ->  bundled/skills/  ->  declared public GitHub source
```

| Flag | Network | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| *(default)* | as needed | Private bundled, public fetched |
| `--offline` | **none at all** | Private bundled only; public skills reported as unavailable |
| `--prefer-network` | yes | Public skills always refreshed from upstream |

Two skills are deliberately never bundled because of size: `img2threejs` (39.9MB) and
`impeccable` (16MB). Both are optional quality gates, not core specialists.

## Files

```
atelier/
├── install.mjs                  installer, agent detection, offline-first resolution
├── deps.json                    dependency manifest for all 118 skills
├── llms.txt                     this file
├── README.md                    full documentation
├── BRAND.md                     naming, palette, voice
├── .claude-plugin/
│   ├── plugin.json              Claude Code manifest
│   └── marketplace.json         marketplace entry
├── .opencode/plugins/atelier.ts opencode plugin
├── skills/                      the 8 routers
├── agents/                      8 cs-* security subagents
├── bundled/skills/              36 private-origin skills, no network needed
└── scripts/inject-install.mjs   regenerates the AI Installation sections
```

## Safety

The installer never overwrites an existing skill without `--force`, never deletes outside the
target root, and cleans up its own temporary clone directory. `--check` writes nothing.
Network access only occurs for skills that are neither installed nor bundled, and never at
all with `--offline`.
